74380-concerning-isabel-carnaby.title: Isabel Carnaby
74380-concerning-isabel-carnaby.creator: Unknown
74380-concerning-isabel-carnaby.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Lord Kesterton smiled. "I am afraid I still babble o' green benches when I get the chance. The House of Commons is like certain women of one's acquaintance: you quarrel with them, and they expect too much from you, and you vow you will enjoy yourself and have nothing more to do with them; but, all the same, they have spoilt your taste for anything else, and they make all other women seem insufferably dull."

arxiv-2011-13667.title: Toward a better understanding of supernova environments: a study of SNe 2004dg and 2012P in NGC 5806 with HST and MUSE 2020 Toward a better understanding of supernova environments: a study of SNe 2004dg and 2012P in NGC 5806 with HST and MUSE – B
arxiv-2011-13667.creator: Ning-Chen Sun, Justyn R. Maund, Paul A. Crowther, Xuan Fang and Emmanouil Zapartas1 Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of Sheffield, Hicks Building, Hounsfield Road, Sheffield S3 7RH, UK2 Key Laboratory of Optical Astronomy, National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of
arxiv-2011-13667.description: Abstract Core-collapse supernovae (SNe) are the inevitable fate of most massive stars. Since most stars form in groups, SN progenitors can be constrained with information of their environments. It remains challenging to accurately analyse the various components in the environment and to correctly identify their relationships with the SN progenitors.

arxiv-2012-01065.title: BSODA : A Bipartite Scalable Framework for Online Disease Diagnosis Conference: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2022; April 25–29, 2022; Virtual Event, Lyon, France. Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2022 (WWW ’22), April 25–29, 2022, Virtual Event, Lyon, France DOI: 10.1145/3485447.351212
arxiv-2012-01065.creator: Weijie He, Xiaohao Mao, Chao Ma, Yu Huang, José Miguel Hernández-Lobato, Ting Chen
arxiv-2012-01065.description: Abstract . A growing number of people are seeking healthcare advice online. Usually, they diagnose their medical conditions based on the symptoms they are experiencing, which is also known as self-diagnosis. From the machine learning perspective, online disease diagnosis is a sequential feature (symptom) selection and classification problem.

arxiv-2106-07630.title: Hierarchically Regularized Deep Forecasting
arxiv-2106-07630.creator: Biswajit Paria, Rajat Sen, Amr Ahmed, Abhimanyu Das
arxiv-2106-07630.description: Abstract Hierarchical forecasting is a key problem in many practical multivariate forecasting applications - the goal is to simultaneously predict a large number of correlated time series that are arranged in a pre-specified aggregation hierarchy. The main challenge is to exploit the hierarchical correlations to simultaneously obtain good prediction accuracy for time series at different levels of the hierarchy.

arxiv-2112-10888.title: Challenges for the 3-3-1 models
arxiv-2112-10888.creator: V. Pleitez
arxiv-2112-10888.description: Abstract The so-called 3-3-1 models have been widely studied in the literature. However, in almost all cases, as with other models, just simplified versions have been considered. On the other hand, the LHC has not neither confirmed nor rejected any model.

arxiv-2410-22378.title: Theory of vibrational Stark effect for adsorbates and diatomic molecules
arxiv-2410-22378.creator: Sang Yang, Jun Cai, Yanxia Chen, Ming Gong
arxiv-2410-22378.description: Abstract Nowadays the vibrational Stark effect (VSE) of adsorbates at the electrochemical interfaces is generally investigated using the Lambert theory, in which the strong electric field across the interfaces can be treated as some kind of perturbation. Lambert found that the VSE arises mainly from the classical effect, and the quantum effect is negligible.

arxiv-2412-15925.title: MiniGPT-Pancreas: Multimodal Large Language Model for Pancreas Cancer Classification and Detection
arxiv-2412-15925.creator: Andrea Moglia, Elia Clement Nastasio, Luca Mainardi, Pietro Cerveri
arxiv-2412-15925.description: Abstract Problem: Pancreas radiological imaging is challenging due to the small size, blurred boundaries, and variability of shape and position of the organ among patients. Goal: In this work we present MiniGPT-Pancreas, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM), as an interactive chatbot to support clinicians in pancreas cancer diagnosis by integrating visual and textual information.

pmc-10636095.title: Visualizing software refactoring using radar charts
pmc-10636095.creator: Abdel-Rahman Al-Ghuwairi, Dimah Al-Fraihat, Yousef Sharrab, Huda Alrashidi, Nouf Almujally, Ahmed Kittaneh, Ahmed Ali
pmc-10636095.description: Refactoring tools have advanced greatly and are being used in many large projects. As a result, a great deal of information is now available about past refactoring and its effects on the source code. However, when multiple refactoring is performed at once, it becomes more difficult to analyze their impact.

pmc-10822940.title: Gut microbiota in combination with blood metabolites reveals characteristics of the disease cluster of coronary artery disease and cognitive impairment: a Mendelian randomization study
pmc-10822940.creator: Shihan Xu, Yanfei Liu, Qing Wang, Fenglan Liu, Yanfang Xian, Fengqin Xu, Yue Liu
pmc-10822940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe coexistence of coronary artery disease (CAD) and cognitive impairment has become a common clinical phenomenon. However, there is currently limited research on the etiology of this disease cluster, discovery of biomarkers, and identification of precise intervention targets.MethodsWe explored the causal connections between gut microbiota, blood metabolites, and the disease cluster of CAD combined with cognitive impairment through two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR).

pmc-12582099.title: Enhancing the use of routine program data for immunization decision-making: The role of coincidence analysis in localized learning and adaptation
pmc-12582099.creator: Abdu A. Adamu, Duduzile Ndwandwe, Olalekan A. Uthman, Charles S. Wiysonge
pmc-12582099.description: Real-world program data, collected through information management systems and activities like supportive supervision, are abundant in many low- and middle-income countries across the world. These data can be harnessed for systems learning to improve immunization decision-making and address disparities in vaccination coverage.

pmc-12714692.title: CENTRA: knowledge-based gene contextuality graphs reveal functional master regulators by centrality and fractality
pmc-12714692.creator: Frank Hause, Alice Wedler, René Keil, Laura Schian, Markus Glaß, Wiebke F Grimm, Oleksandr Sorokin, Wolfgang Hoehenwarter, Andrea Sinz, Stefan Hüttelmaier
pmc-12714692.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Deciphering gene function via context-aware approaches is limited by various means. Especially, static gene sets used in enrichment analyses and the lack of single-gene resolution restrain flexible association of genes with specific contexts. Here, we introduce CENTRA (Centrality-Based Exploration of Network Topologies from Regulatory Assemblies), a framework that models gene contextuality through topic-specific gene co-occurrence networks derived from curated gene sets and associated literature.

pmc-12821705.title: Reading Music or Reading Notes? Rethinking Musical Stimuli in Eye-Movement Research
pmc-12821705.creator: Katarzyna Julia Leikvoll
pmc-12821705.description: This article examines the nature of musical stimuli used in eye-movement research on music reading, with a focus on syntactic elements essential for fluent reading: melody, rhythm, and harmony. Drawing parallels between language and music as syntactic systems, the study critiques the widespread use of stimuli that lack coherent musical structure, such as random pitch sequences or rhythmically ambiguous patterns.

pmc-13342117.title: Deep learning-based prediction of 24-2 visual field from fundus photographs in glaucoma
pmc-13342117.creator: Keunheung Park, Hwayeong Kim, Sangwoo Moon, Jiwoong Lee
pmc-13342117.description: PurposeTo develop a deep learning architecture for predicting visual field (VF) maps from fundus images.MethodsFundus images and VF test results were obtained from two tertiary hospitals. The training dataset comprised 31,443 fundus photographs and 27,364 VF examinations, whereas the test dataset comprised 6,436 fundus photographs and 5,647 VF examinations.

pmc-13458861.title: Global country-level network analysis of mental disorders
pmc-13458861.creator: Mohammadreza Balooch Hasankhani, Shoboo Rahmati, Mark J.M. Sullman, Tania Dehesh, Herbert Ainamani, Prodyut Roy, Prodyut Roy, Herbert Ainamani, Prodyut Roy
pmc-13458861.description: Content of image described in text. Impact statement Mental disorders account for a substantial share of ill health globally, yet cross-country patterns in their incidence are rarely examined jointly. Using GBD 2023 country-level estimates, we mapped a regularized ecological network of 10 mental disorders and the sociodemographic Index across 204 countries and territories.

pmc-13575816.title: Quantification in bone SPECT/CT
pmc-13575816.creator: Jovana Zivanovic, Jules Zhang-Yin
pmc-13575816.description: BackgroundQuantitative bone SPECT/CT enables objective assessment of skeletal radiotracer uptake using standardised uptake values (SUVs) and related parameters. Advances in reconstruction, correction methods, calibration and detector technology have improved measurement reliability and expanded interest in oncological and benign skeletal applications. This review evaluates current clinical applications, technical limitations and future directions of quantitative bone SPECT/CT.
